clue.text: Novelist's party number ()

parts.note: a rave is a large lively party

explanation.surface: A novelist's party piece, perhaps a song at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Raven was an English novelist, author of the Alms for Oblivion sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Raven was a twentieth-century English writer of fiction.

clue.text: Compassion (a modicum) for Pecksniff's pupil's wife

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or compassion
a pinch is a tiny amount, a modicum

explanation.surface: A little compassion for the wife of a pupil of the hypocritical Pecksniff.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit, Tom Pinch's sister Ruth marries John Westlock, once a pupil of Pecksniff.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's character Ruth Pinch marries John Westlock, Pecksniff's former pupil, in Martin Chuzzlewit.

clue.text: Periodical rage

definitions.meaning: a periodical is a magazine, here the fashion monthly of that name
the rage means the current fashion or craze

explanation.definitionFit: Vogue is a famous fashion magazine, and to be in vogue is to be the rage, the fashion.

clue.text: An account of Gertrude Stein

parts.note: reads as a biography of the writer, but points to her 1935 lectures, whose title is a word for an account

explanation.surface: A biographical account of the American writer Gertrude Stein.
explanation.definitionFit: Stein's lecture series published in 1935 bears a title meaning the telling of a story or account.

clue.text: Has German composer been vet? Oh, possibly.

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged in another order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the great composer had once trained as a vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BEEN, VET and OH; 'Has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwig van Beethoven, born in Bonn, was a German composer.

clue.text: Poet's connections

definitions.meaning: spans that join two sides, links between places or people

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bridges was an English Poet Laureate, and links across rivers or between ideas are spans of that name.

clue.text: Joy was its daughter, wrote Schiller

definitions.text: Joy was its daughter, wrote Schiller

parts.words: Joy was its daughter, wrote Schiller
parts.note: in the Ode to Joy, Schiller calls Joy the daughter of the paradise of the blessed

explanation.surface: Schiller writing that Joy was the offspring of some place.
explanation.walkthrough: Schiller's Ode to Joy, set by Beethoven, opens 'Freude, schöner Götterfunken, Tochter aus Elysium'.
explanation.definitionFit: Schiller's ode names Joy as 'Tochter aus Elysium', daughter of the Greek paradise of heroes.

clue.text: He figured in early comedy denouement by the seat of his pants

definitions.text: He figured in early comedy denouement by the seat of his pants

parts.words: He figured in early comedy denouement by the seat of his pants
parts.note: a character in the early English comedy Gammer Gurton's Needle, where the lost needle turns up in the seat of a servant's breeches

explanation.surface: Someone improvising the ending of an early comedy by the seat of his pants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the seat of his pants' sounds like the idiom for improvising, but in Gammer Gurton's Needle the lost needle is literally found in the seat of Hodge's breeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Hodge is the servant in Gammer Gurton's Needle, an early English comedy, in whose breeches the needle is found.

clue.text: One of Thackeray's colonials

parts.note: Thackeray's novel about the Warrington twins from an American colony is named after its people

explanation.surface: A colonial figure from one of Thackeray's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's novel The Virginians follows two brothers from the American colony of Virginia.

clue.text: Scandinavian mistresses of spin

parts.note: suggests women skilled in political spin, but means the Norse goddesses who spin the threads of fate

explanation.surface: Scandinavian women who are experts at political spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' suggests public relations; the Norse Fates spin the thread of every life.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the three Fates who weave and spin destiny are called the Norns.

clue.text: "Peter Pan save me, me his velly nice friend"

definitions.text: "Peter Pan save me, me his velly nice friend"

parts.words: "Peter Pan save me, me his velly nice friend"
parts.note: the words of the chief's daughter rescued by Peter in Barrie's play, in her broken English

explanation.surface: A quotation in pidgin English from someone rescued by Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Barrie's Peter Pan the princess saved by Peter at Marooners' Rock speaks these words.

clue.text: Engraver of the French resistance, with some hesitation

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
er is the sound of a hesitation

explanation.surface: An engraver in the French Resistance who hesitated a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with some' just links the hesitation to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance master of woodcuts and copperplate engravings.

clue.text: Holy picture initiates painter into early Tuscan art ()

indicators.note: initiates here means the opening letters, those that start each of the following words

explanation.surface: A painter introducing a sacred image into early Tuscan art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiates' looks like a verb, but it names the initial letters of 'painter into early Tuscan art'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, a devotional image.

clue.text: Abducted prince as courier on Rhode Island (America)

parts.note: a courier leads tourists, a guide
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A kidnapped prince working as a courier in Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Cymbeline, the king's sons Guiderius and Arviragus were stolen as infants by Belarius.
explanation.definitionFit: Guiderius is Cymbeline's son, carried off in infancy and raised in a Welsh cave in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Bathing beauties tangled in reeds

indicators.note: tangled signals that the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Swimmers caught up in the reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' rearranges IN REEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nereids are sea nymphs of Greek myth, lovely maidens who live in the water.

clue.text: Some classic tremors exhibited by writers like Burns and Blake

definitions.text: Some classic tremors exhibited by writers like Burns and Blake

parts.words: Some classic tremors exhibited by writers like Burns and Blake
parts.note: the poets who reacted against classicism sent tremors through the classical tradition

explanation.surface: Burns and Blake showing signs of nervous shaking in their verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns and Blake are forerunners of the movement that overturned eighteenth-century classical taste, causing tremors among classicists.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns and Blake are counted among the early poets of the late-eighteenth-century movement opposed to classicism.

clue.text: Chap protects damaged Mir in epic poem

indicators.note: protects means the first piece shelters, so goes around, the second

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the Russian space station Mir, whose letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A man shielding the damaged Mir space station in a long poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' puts the chap round the scrambled station, signalled by 'damaged'; the printed Mir lacks the O the answer needs, a slip by the setter. Mir was the Russian space station.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmion is Walter Scott's long narrative poem of Flodden Field, an epic in verse.

clue.text: Version of Circe in rare form of fugue

indicators.note: in places the rearranged piece inside the other word
a version of a word here is a rearranged form of its letters

explanation.surface: A rare version of the Circe story set as a fugue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Version of' signals the anagram of the enchantress's name, and 'in' sets it inside the adjective; the surface reads Circe as Homer's sorceress.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricercare is an elaborate contrapuntal instrumental piece, a precursor of the fugue.

clue.text: Mackenzie's boreal element of love

parts.note: A boreal element is the cold blast from the north

explanation.surface: A chilly, northern side to love, as Mackenzie described it.
explanation.definitionFit: Boreal means northern, and the moving air from that direction is named in Compton Mackenzie's title.

clue.text: Namesake of Roman fellow, friend of Pistol

parts.note: homo is Latin for man
Nym is a companion of Pistol and Bardolph in Shakespeare's history plays

explanation.surface: A Roman man who shares a name with a crony of Pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A word spelt like another but of different meaning shares its name, so is its namesake.

clue.text: "I mean by a 'vocabulary' one in which no word can be defined in terms of the others" (Bertrand Russell)

definitions.text: "I mean by a 'vocabulary' one in which no word can be defined in terms of the others" (Bertrand Russell)

parts.words: "I mean by a 'vocabulary' one in which no word can be defined in terms of the others" (Bertrand Russell)
parts.note: Russell's definition of the smallest possible vocabulary, from Human Knowledge, with the qualifying word omitted

explanation.surface: Bertrand Russell defining what he means by a vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Russell called the smallest set of words from which all others can be defined a vocabulary of this kind.

clue.text: German books with new content reveal shortlived dramatist

indicators.note: content is what a thing holds, so the letter is held inside the other piece

parts.note: Bücher is the German word for books

explanation.surface: German books with fresh material revealing a playwright who died young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new content' puts N inside BUCHER; 'reveal' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Büchner, author of Woyzeck, was a German playwright who died aged twenty-three.

clue.text: English travel writer acquires new heart for Australian poet

indicators.note: acquires means the writer's name takes the letter into its middle

parts.note: Gerald Brenan wrote South from Granada about life in Spain

explanation.surface: An English travel writer given a new heart for an Australian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquires new heart' puts N into the middle of BRENAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Brennan was a Symbolist poet from Sydney.

clue.text: Lake girl in lawyer's account

definitions.meaning: the lake on the Rhine bordering Germany, Austria and Switzerland
the heroine of Chaucer's Man of Law's Tale

explanation.definitionFit: Lake Constance lies on the Rhine, and the Man of Law's Tale in Chaucer tells of the virtuous princess of that name.

clue.text: Browning's smiling boy fell dead beside him ()

definitions.text: Browning's smiling boy fell dead beside him

parts.words: Browning's smiling boy fell dead beside him
parts.note: in Incident of the French Camp the wounded boy falls dead smiling beside Napoleon, his leader

explanation.surface: A line about a boy dying with a smile, from a Browning poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem ends 'And his chief beside, / Smiling the boy fell dead.'
explanation.definitionFit: Browning's poem calls Napoleon the boy's leader or commander, the word that ends the line.

clue.text: Lord Jim and Lady Windermere are each one, and each are found in one

definitions.text: Lord Jim and Lady Windermere are each one, and each are found in one

parts.words: Lord Jim and Lady Windermere are each one, and each are found in one
parts.note: Lord Jim names a novel and Lady Windermere's Fan a play, while Lord and Lady are themselves forms of rank

explanation.surface: Two fictional aristocrats compared as kinds of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Each name is a book or play name, and 'Lord' and 'Lady' within them are ranks of nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Jim and Lady Windermere's Fan are names of works, and Lord and Lady are ranks of nobility.

clue.text: Golding leader in moral philosophy

indicators.note: in shows the name lies within the words moral philosophy

explanation.surface: William Golding as a leading figure in moral philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lord of the Flies the boys elect Ralph as their leader.
explanation.definitionFit: In Golding's Lord of the Flies the stranded boys choose Ralph as chief.

clue.text: Browning's autobiographical dawn girl ()

parts.note: Elizabeth Barrett Browning's verse novel Aurora ... has a heroine whose first name means dawn

explanation.surface: A girl at daybreak in a poem drawn from Browning's own life.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora, Latin for dawn, is the heroine of Elizabeth Barrett Browning's partly autobiographical Aurora Leigh.

clue.text: Dostoevsky's mature version of Wordsworth's boy? ()

definitions.text: Dostoevsky's mature version of Wordsworth's boy?

parts.words: Dostoevsky's mature version of Wordsworth's boy?
parts.note: Dostoevsky's novel about Prince Myshkin shares a word with Wordsworth's ballad The ... Boy

explanation.surface: Dostoevsky writing a grown-up version of a Wordsworth child.
explanation.definitionFit: Dostoevsky's novel is The Idiot, and Wordsworth wrote The Idiot Boy, so the novel's hero is the boy grown up.

clue.text: He "married on his whiskers, upon which property he had previously subsisted"

definitions.text: He "married on his whiskers, upon which property he had previously subsisted"

parts.words: He "married on his whiskers, upon which property he had previously subsisted"
parts.note: Dickens's description in Nicholas Nickleby of the dressmaker's foppish husband

explanation.surface: A man who lived off his good looks and married on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens says this of Mr Mantalini, the idle, extravagant husband of Madame Mantalini in Nicholas Nickleby.

clue.text: West's compleatly shod angler?

parts.note: 'compleatly' nods to Walton's The Compleat Angler

explanation.surface: A fully booted angler in the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: West is the novelist Morris West, not a direction; his pope wears the 'shoes' of St Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris West's novel The Shoes of the Fisherman puts footwear on an angler, the pope as heir to St Peter.

clue.text: Hoped to make an ancient vestment

indicators.note: to make signals that the letters are used to build something new

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to sew an ancient garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges HOPED.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephod is an apron-like garment worn by Jewish high priests in ancient times.
